question.question: Can a batched LogDB suffix append return success while replacing its already-saved, nonoverlapping prefix after an uncached batch read returns a non-notfound error?
question.importance: Silent loss of prior stored log entries can undermine the history used for recovery and term matching. The selected responsibility is the storage boundary; no end-to-end consensus violation is assumed.
question.trigger_rationale: Exploration 6015c2ed7f9b493e8e1194edbbd96796 observed success with prefix [1,2,3] removed after a single injected read error, whereas the control retained it. Source explicitly collapses read errors into batch absence. A separately fixed comparison can test successful-save prefix preservation without requiring proof of global consequence.

obligation.description: For batched LogDB with an already-saved prefix and no intervening deletion or compaction, a later nonoverlapping suffix append that returns success must preserve the previous prefix entries and their terms/payloads. A failed required backing read may be reported as failure; it must not turn a successful append into deletion of the unsupplied prefix.

scope.description: Batched storage boundary, uncached partial-batch append after reopening, with one non-notfound GetValue error and otherwise successful KV operations.
assumptions: Earlier save succeeded and its prefix is read back before the append.
Append supplies indices strictly beyond the prior prefix and requests no deletion, compaction or snapshot.
KV read error is an explicit injected interface outcome; the underlying existing bytes remain intact until target code writes.
excluded: No physical-device failure frequency or reachability claim.
No end-to-end Raft quorum, election, application or crash-consensus violation is asserted.
Plain entry format, cached merge and aligned batch appends are not this scenario.

grounding.derivation: ILogDB atomically saves the supplied updates and exposes continuous saved entries; KV.GetValue can return an error, and the actual Pebble adapter propagates non-notfound errors. TestGetMergedFirstBatch independently requires the old first index and earlier terms to survive a suffix merge. Hence a successful append is not licensed to erase untouched earlier entries merely because its prerequisite read failed. Returning an error remains permitted, so the oracle is success implies preservation, not unconditional success. This requirement is confined to the documented storage interface with an explicit injected error, not a claim that CFT network faults include arbitrary disk corruption.
grounding.applicability: Uncached first-batch merge in explicitly selected batched format, with readable prefix before operation and subsequent read-back after fault injection ends.

bindings.description: Converts both missing key and non-notfound backing read errors to the same false result used by first-batch merge.

feedback.answered: Conditional exploration completed: after reopen both controls read the saved prefix [1,2,3]. Appending entry 4 without fault returned success and stored [1,2,3,4]. With one injected non-notfound read error, save still returned success but the backing batch contained only [4]. The exact interface-return substitution is retained; no physical error producer or consensus cluster executed. The independently grounded obligation checks only success implying prefix preservation.
